entry.title: Added Bruin’s USD 10,000 Cloud credit for YC-, Techstars-, or Antler-backed teams; separated the two-year product credit from free tools and a waitlist for nonqualifying founders. Rechecked Interledger pause and NLnet deadline.
Added PostHog startup credits for eligible young companies and separated the USD 50,000 headline from five AI tools excluded since 14 September 2026. Rechecked Interledger pause and NLnet deadline.

Added Stripe Atlas fee credits for companies formed through its paid Delaware service. USD 2,500 offsets eligible Stripe fees for one year but cannot pay the USD 500 setup or later agent renewal. Rechecked Interledger pause and NLnet deadline.

Clarified that Google Scale excludes more than USD 5,000 in prior Cloud credits, so the published Start maximum does not alone close Scale; added funding, round-age, two-year coverage and no-guarantee limits.

Changed the Interledger Local Impact Mini-Grants from an announced 11 November rolling window to paused after the current programme page and application form posted a pause. Kept historical terms, award limits, and official links; no reopening date is published.

Added the EIC Accelerator 2026 route with the 4 November full-proposal batch, prior short-stage GO, first-stage packet, 4–6-week normal feedback, grant-versus-investment distinction, and country uncertainty.

Rechecked NLnet’s 3 November Open Internet Stack call, EUR 5,000–50,000 first-grant range, Restack AI-project exclusion, and current GenAI disclosure rule. The announced policy revision remains unknown.

Added GitHub for Startups: USD 10,000 in Enterprise-platform credits for eligible funded, partner-affiliated startups. The catalogue keeps the outside-funding, prior-plan, prior-benefit, payment-method, 12-month, data-residency, and post-credit-billing limits next to the amount, and marks country coverage, full eligible usage, post-credit price, and approval time as unknown.

Added Interledger Foundation’s USD 500–3,000 Local Impact Mini-Grants for individual practitioners, unregistered groups, and local fintech startups with a defined financial-access project. The catalogue keeps the 11 November deadline, sanctions restriction, application packet, direct-activity budget boundary, six-month delivery condition, and missing award or selection terms beside the range.

Added The Pollination Project’s rolling global seed-grant route for individual project applicants, with its USD 500 ceiling, project-size and unpaid-work limits, payment and reporting duties, month-end completeness rule, and missing selection or country-map terms beside the offer.

Added Awesome Foundation DC’s current USD 1,000 local cash-grant route for individual projects. The catalogue keeps the Washington, DC benefit, near-term project, tangible-impact, and discretionary-selection gates beside the award and marks the current cutoff, residency rule, selection rate, and award guarantee as unknown.

Added GitHub Student Developer Pack’s current USD 25 Stripe fee-credit route for verified students. The catalogue keeps the student-verification gate, separate payment-fee purpose, partner-controlled and changing terms, and missing Stripe account, country, coverage, expiry, and post-credit-fee details beside the amount.

Added GitHub Student Developer Pack’s current Heroku route for verified students: USD 13 in credit per month for 24 months. The catalogue now keeps enrollment proof, personal-account and age gates, non-stacking or repeat-claim limits, changing partner terms, and missing Heroku billing details beside the amount.

Added Oracle Cloud Free Tier as an individual route: US$300 in eligible OCI credits for 30 days plus Always Free services. The catalogue now keeps select-country availability, card verification, the irreversible Home Region choice, capacity limits, and post-credit resource outcome beside the amount.

Refreshed Microsoft for Startups: its direct no-referral path is verified, but current official pages state USD 200 and USD 1,000 starter credits. The direct amount is now shown as Unknown; the USD 150,000 figure is separated as a staged ceiling, with review and billing boundaries beside it.

Added Open Technology Fund’s rolling individual internet-freedom grant, with its USD 10,000–900,000 range, project-scope, sanctions, Concept Note, response estimate, and performance-contract gates. Refreshed Cloudflare’s caps, exclusions, payment method, overage, post-expiry billing, and review terms while preserving its unresolved Tier 3 funding conflict.

Added DigitalOcean Startups as a route a founder can submit without a VC, incubator, or accelerator, while keeping its unpublished direct-applicant award, 12-month term, eligibility gates, GPU and third-party AI exclusions, and allocation uncertainty visible.

Added UKRI’s sustainable-AI research opportunity for eligible individual applicants and research groups, with its UK research-organisation host gate, 10 November deadline, and GBP 602,500 full-economic-cost ceiling distinguished from a personal grant.

Added MongoDB for Startups as a direct route for eligible Series A-or-earlier companies, with its public website and LinkedIn gates, two 12-month credit clocks, and the unambiguous unknown: MongoDB does not publish the base-tier credit amount.
Updated AWS Activate: Founders now carries its public-website gate and issuer-published 5–10-business-day decision window; Portfolio retains its Provider Organization ID gate and USD 200,000 ceiling.
